title: 22.3 A 42Gb/s Single-Ended Hybrid-DFE PAM-3 Receiver for GDDR7 Memory Interfaces
problem: GDDR7 PAM3 receivers must achieve 42Gb/s while managing inter-symbol interference (ISI) and tight feedback timing constraints in direct-feedback (DF) DFE implementations.
motivation: As GDDR7 targets data-rates of 28Gb/s and higher with PAM3 signaling, ISI becomes more severe and feedback timing closure becomes increasingly difficult for traditional DFE designs.
method: The receiver detects 42 billion bits per second on graphics memory (GDDR7) using three signal levels (PAM-3). Because each bit's signal is distorted by previous bits (inter-symbol interference), it uses a decision feedback equalizer — subtracting out the known interference from already-detected bits. To do this fast enough, the design combines two approaches: direct-feedback, which uses only the immediately previous bit for fast response, and loop-unrolled detection (calculating several future bits in parallel instead of one at a time). This hybrid approach delivers fast feedback timing without the silicon and power cost of fully parallel detection.
key_novelty: It combines fast single-bit feedback with partial parallel detection of future bits to achieve 42Gb/s without the full area and power cost of detecting all bits at once.
contributions: Hybrid DFE architecture combining direct-feedback and loop-unrolled approaches
Reduced feedback time to within 1UI at 42Gb/s
Minimized area and power overhead vs pure LU-DFE
limitations: Abstract-only analysis; specific area/power comparisons and timing margins not quantified.
primary_theme: Hybrid DFE for high-speed PAM3 memory receivers
